blocks.heading: Symbol Ledger and Domain Conventions
blocks.text: This section owns the formal symbol domain for the candidate mechanism. The gravitational mass M and spin period P are operationalized in solar masses and milliseconds respectively, serving as the dependent variables for the mass-spin relation. The causal speed limit check c enforces the dimensionless constraint c_s <= c on the dense matter equation of state. The evolutionary channel A3 distinguishes between isolated magnetic-dipole spin-down and binary recycling. The relaxed static equilibrium axioms A1 and the binary accretion support mechanism A2 act as the primary independent perturbations. The derived relation R(P) maps the spin period to the gravitational mass. These symbols form the basis for the candidate propositions and proof obligations, with their operational definitions requiring human review to resolve the specific mathematical relaxation conditions.

The numbered relation defines the candidate mass-spin function R. It posits that the gravitational mass M is a function of the spin period P, modulated by the relaxed equilibrium axioms A1, the binary accretion support A2, and the evolutionary channel A3. This relation is the central object of the formal derivation. The specific functional form of R is currently undefined and requires formal specification, as noted in the unresolved inputs.

blocks.heading: Candidate Lemma Registry
blocks.text: The theory spine defines eight candidate lemmas (L1-L8) that structure the forward derivation. L1 and L2 are candidate formalizations of the primary propositions P1 and P2. L3 represents the proposed application of the relaxation to the static equilibrium constraint. L4 through L8 are unverified lemmas that attempt to derive the existence of R(P), evaluate the mass limit, check the causality bound, assess the evolutionary channel, and distinguish the pulsar classes. These lemmas are strictly unverified and depend on the resolution of the formal definitions.

blocks.heading: Candidate Propositions
blocks.text: P1 proposes that relaxing the static equilibrium axioms of the dense matter equation of state with rotational and thermal support permits masses beyond the static Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff limit without violating the causality bound. P2 proposes that these relaxed axioms predict a distinct mass-spin relation R(P) that distinguishes massive neutron stars (M > 2.0 solar masses) with millisecond periods from isolated magnetic-dipole spin-down pulsars. Both propositions are candidate formalizations and remain unverified pending the resolution of the proof obligations.

blocks.heading: Dependency and Failure Condition Matrix
blocks.text:
| Proof Obligation | Required Lemmas | Failure Condition | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| PO1 | L1, L3, L4, L6 | Relaxed axioms violate causality bound (c_s > c) | needs_human_input |
| PO2 | L2, L5, L7, L8 | Predicted R(P) contradicts observed massive MSP population | needs_human_input |

The dependency matrix maps the proof obligations to the candidate lemmas. PO1 fails if the relaxation in A1 inevitably violates the causal speed limit c. PO2 fails if the derived relation R(P) does not produce the expected mass-spin separation for the evolutionary channel A3. Both obligations are currently unverified.

blocks.heading: Assumption Ledger
blocks.text:
The formal argument rests on three candidate assumptions:
1. A1: Static equilibrium axioms can be relaxed to permit mass accumulation beyond the TOV limit via rotational and thermal support without violating causality.
2. A2: Binary mass accretion and angular momentum transfer can be modeled as a continuous thermodynamic and mechanical perturbation modifying effective equilibrium conditions.
3. A3: Companion ablation primarily affects the surface and magnetosphere, allowing the core mass-spin relation to remain governed by the relaxed effective equilibrium axioms.
These assumptions require human review to establish their mathematical rigor.
